findings.title: Stored XSS: remotely fetched HTML is rendered unescaped in the embed view
findings.body: The view renders posts with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and TopicEmbed.import (app/models/topic_embed.rb:22) creates those posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which makes Post#cook return the raw string verbatim, skipping Discourse's entire sanitization/whitelist pipeline. The content originates from a remote page or RSS feed fetched by TopicEmbed.import_remote / Jobs::PollFeed. Any HTML on the embedded site (including user-generated comments on a blog, or a compromised/attacker-controlled page on the allowed host) — `<script>`, inline event handlers, etc. — is therefore stored and served as-is from the Discourse origin inside the /embed/best iframe. Because the iframe is same-origin with the forum, injected JavaScript runs with full access to the viewer's Discourse session (cookie theft, posting as the user, admin actions if a staff member views the embed). The remote content must be sanitized (e.g. with Sanitize/Nokogiri whitelist) before being stored, or rendered on a separate origin.

findings.title: embed_url is interpolated unescaped into an HTML anchor in imported posts
findings.body:
`contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "` interpolates the URL directly into an HTML attribute delimited by single quotes. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?://` (line 11), which does not exclude quotes. A URL such as `http://host/' onmouseover='alert(1)` (URL-encoded appropriately in the feed item or embed_url param) passes the regex, breaks out of the href attribute, and injects arbitrary attributes/HTML. Since the post is cooked with cook_method raw_html and rendered via `raw`, this is a stored XSS on the Discourse origin. The URL must be HTML-escaped (or the anchor built with Nokogiri) before insertion.

findings.title: request.referer interpolated unescaped into inline JavaScript
findings.body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` inserts the raw Referer header into a `<script>` block with no JavaScript or HTML escaping. The Referer header is fully attacker-controlled; the only gate is that `URI(request.referer).host` must equal `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (EmbedController#ensure_embeddable). Ruby's URI parser accepts single quotes and other characters in the path, so a Referer like `http://embeddable.host/');alert(1);//` passes the host check and terminates the string literal in the generated script, allowing arbitrary JavaScript injection into the embed page (which is same-origin with the forum). The value must be JSON-escaped (e.g. `to_json`) or passed via a data attribute.

findings.title: A background job is enqueued on every embed request for an unknown URL, with throttling only inside the job
findings.body: When no TopicEmbed exists for the requested embed_url, `best` enqueues a `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job on every (uncached) request. The 60-second Redis throttle lives inside TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?, i.e. inside the job — it does nothing to limit enqueue volume. A busy site embedding comments (or any client that spoofs the Referer) will enqueue one Sidekiq job per page view for the same URL, flooding the queue and the Redis setnx key space (`retrieved:<url>` keys are never cleaned beyond the 60s expire, and the URL is unbounded user input). The throttle should be applied before enqueueing (e.g. in the controller, checking the Redis key), or the job should be deduplicated.

findings.title: RetrieveTopic job runs the entire PollFeed import synchronously inline
findings.body: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` invokes the full feed polling job inline within the RetrieveTopic worker, rather than enqueuing it. This means a single embed page view for an unknown URL triggers a synchronous fetch and import of the entire RSS/ATOM feed inside that job: it can run for a long time, can run concurrently with the hourly scheduled PollFeed (both checking `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:)` before either commits, leading to duplicate topic creation attempts that blow up on the unique index), and bypasses the job's sidekiq_options (retry: false). PollFeed should be enqueued as a job, or a shared lock should serialize feed imports.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content, and failures are swallowed by retry: false
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item responds to `content` with a non-nil value. SimpleRSS returns nil for missing elements (many RSS feeds have no `content`/`content:encoded` element), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll loop — items after the offending one are never imported. Combined with `sidekiq_options retry: false` (line 12), a single malformed item permanently breaks feed importing each hour with no retry. Guard for nil content, and rescue per-item errors so one bad entry doesn't halt the entire poll. Also note `feed_key` (line 20) is dead code — it is never used, so the intended modified-since/conditional-fetch logic is not implemented.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` is invalid ERB — the template fails or behaves unpredictably when rendered
findings.body: Line 6 closes the header's if/else with `<%- end if %>`. The trailing `if` is not valid: it generates `end if` in the compiled Ruby with no condition on the tag, which depending on how ERB lays out the generated source either raises a SyntaxError at render time or consumes the next emitted statement as a bogus modifier-if condition, scrambling output order. No test renders this template (the controller specs stub TopicView.new and never render the view), so the breakage is invisible to CI. The tag should be `<%- end %>`, and a request/view spec that actually renders the embed response is needed.

findings.title: `create_table ... force: true` silently drops an existing table during migration
findings.body: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` drops any pre-existing `topic_embeds` table without warning before recreating it. In production (e.g. re-running migrations, restoring a partial schema, or a table left from a prior deploy) this silently destroys data. The same `force: true` was also added to the already-shipped migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3`, which is additionally a no-op/divergence risk: installations that already ran that migration will never see the change, so the codebase's migration history no longer matches what exists in those databases. Drop `force: true` from both migrations.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx/expire can leave a permanent throttle key, blocking future retrievals
findings.body: `retrieved_recently?` performs `$redis.setnx(key, '1')` and then, only if it succeeded, `$redis.expire(key, 60)` in a separate round trip. If the process dies (or the Redis connection drops) between the two calls, the key is set with no TTL and persists forever — from then on `retrieved_recently?` returns true for that embed_url and the topic is never retrieved again, permanently showing the loading view. Use a single atomic command (`$redis.set(key, '1', nx: true, ex: 60)` or setex-based pattern).

findings.title: Origin check uses substring indexOf instead of exact origin match
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts a message from any origin that merely appears as a substring of the configured discourseUrl. For example, with `discourseUrl = 'http://forum.example.com'`, an attacker origin `http://forum.example.com.attacker.com` (or any URL containing that string) passes the check and can drive `iframe.height`. The impact is limited to resizing the embed iframe, but the check should compare origins exactly: `e.origin === discourseUrl` (normalized, e.g. trailing slash stripped).

findings.title: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a valid header value
findings.body: "ALLOWALL" is not part of the X-Frame-Options specification (valid values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN, and ALLOW-FROM in some browsers). Browsers that don't recognize the value ignore the header, which happens to permit framing here, but other browsers/proxies may treat the malformed header conservatively and block the embed, and the intent is unclear to anyone maintaining the code. Use `X-Frame-Options: ALLOW-FROM <host>` (with its caveats) or, better, a CSP `frame-ancestors` policy listing the embeddable host.
